    • Constructor Detail

      • SlimefunItemStack

        public SlimefunItemStack(@Nonnull
                         java.lang.String id,
                         @Nonnull
                         org.bukkit.inventory.ItemStack item)
        Implementation Note:
        Every SlimefunItemStack, regardless of which constructor built it, ends up with its display name set to the raw id and no lore: the persisted stack must never carry baked player-facing text (see the "name is always the id" rule). Per-viewer name/lore is produced at render time by the packet translation layer (PacketItemRewriter), which resolves it from the id. The one exception is isInternalChromeId(String).

      • SlimefunItemStack

        public SlimefunItemStack(@Nonnull
                         java.lang.String id,
                         @Nonnull
                         org.bukkit.Material type)
        The preferred, resource-driven constructor: the item carries only its id and Material. Its display name and lore come from languages/en/items.yml (name + block lore: type/description/stats/usage), applied by the ItemTranslationService English baseline pass after items load. This keeps ALL English text out of the code and in the resources, where it can be translated and follow the unified block-lore structure. New items should use this constructor and author their entry in en/items.yml rather than passing a hardcoded name/lore.

      • getTranslationKey

        @Deprecated
public java.lang.String getTranslationKey()
        Deprecated. 
        Implementation Note:
        Java-8 port: this method and the ItemStack methods below it mirror modern Paper APIs that are absent at the 1.8.8 compile floor. Their bodies go through ReflectionCompat so they fully work on modern servers and degrade gracefully (null / sensible default) on legacy ones. Signatures use compileOnly-stubbed Paper/Adventure types; the Object-to-generic casts are unchecked by nature (hence the @SuppressWarnings).
